business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
New Zealand-Australia Closer Economic Relations Trade Agreement and associated Investment Protocol
Convention between New Zealand and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), as amended; Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), as amended by the Companies (Ultimate Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023; Counter-Terrorism Act 2004, as amended; Sanctions Act 2019, as amended; and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2015, which impose identification and verification duties on registered agents and company service providers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand notary public, followed by Apostille issued by the MFAT Authentication Unit under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, the document must undergo consular legalization at that state's New Zealand consulate after MFAT verification; the apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand notary public, then Apostille by the MFAT Authentication Unit under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961. For non-Apostille destination states, use consular legalization at the destination consulate after MFAT verification; these two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the registered agent and any foreign representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD, authenticated by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Resolution signed by the board, witnessed and notarized by a New Zealand notary public, then Apostille by the MFAT Authentication Unit for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, use consular legalization at the destination consulate after notarization and MFAT authentication. No sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary and founding shareholders, filed with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified conformed copy notarized by a New Zealand notary public, then Apostille by MFAT for Hague Convention states; consular legalization only for states not party to the Apostille Convention, following MFAT verification. The two paths are alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a qualifying New Zealand banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing New Zealand bank or financial institution holding a valid license under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signatory signature verified by the New Zealand bank's authorized officer, then notarized by a New Zealand notary public and Apostilled by MFAT for Apostille member states; for non-member states, use consular legalization at the destination consulate after notarization and MFAT authentication. The routes remain strictly mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial ownership layer, trust settlor, protector, and any holder of power of attorney must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated list, New Zealand sanctions regulations under the Sanctions Act 2019, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, HM Treasury sanctions, the World Bank debarment list, and domestic law enforcement databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and immediate family or close associates. The screening process must be conducted at inception, refreshed within 5 business days before incorporation, and repeated continuously through automated sanctions monitoring. All screenings must be documented using verifiable legal identifiers such as passport, national identity card, or company registration number, with investment documentation retained for at least 10 years under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Business Name Reservation Online Service (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Latin alphabet; no Chinese characters or logographic script may form part of the registered legal name. The name must be English-language or a recognized phonetic transliteration of a foreign trademark. New Zealand law applies a four-tier distinction: (1) identical names, (2) names that are substantially similar or phonetically indistinguishable, (3) names that are confusingly similar to existing registered names or reserved names, and (4) names requiring ministerial or regulatory approval because they contain sensitive words or imply government patronage.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days after the date of the Companies Office name rejection notice, the applicant or its authorized registered agent may file a formal reconsideration request using the prescribed Companies Office form, attaching a statutory declaration that demonstrates the proposed name is not identical, not substantially similar, and not confusingly similar to any protected or reserved name. The declaration must also state that the name does not imply a false connection with government, royal bodies, financial services, or professional bodies. The Registrar of Companies will issue a written administrative decision. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under sections 370 to 371 of the Companies Act 1993, or apply for judicial review on the record. No name extension is permitted beyond the original 20-working-day reservation; instead, a fresh reservation application is required once the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the statutory registered office of a New Zealand company because section 189 of the Companies Act 1993 requires a registered office to be a physical address within New Zealand where documents can be served during ordinary business hours. Furthermore, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand commercial banks generally reject a virtual-office-only arrangement for an offshore secretarial and company administration business because it lacks operational substance, local decision-making capacity, and personnel. A serviced professional suite with a dedicated physical desk, file storage, personnel, meeting space, and signage can meet the registered office and commercial substance threshold, provided it is not merely a postal forwarding point and is included in the company's books and records as the head office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections by local municipal authorities and the Companies Office are moderately likely for a registered-agent industry entity. Quantified risk: approximately 15% probability within the first 12 months of operation. Checklist: (1) physical signage consistent with the registered name; (2) an office that is open to public service during working hours; (3) a named employee who can produce governance registers; (4) lease or occupancy documents matching the registered address; (5) GST, payroll, and corporate tax records available for audit; (6) customer due diligence files stored on premises or accessible through a controlled data room; (7) fire safety and building compliance certificates. If a virtual mailbox is used in an attempt to satisfy the registered office requirement, the probability of an adverse inspection finding is 85%; using a properly staffed serviced office reduces that risk to 5%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: New Zealand Companies Office statutory fees for name reservation and company incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed fee schedule under the Companies Act 1993 and the Ministry of Justice fees regulations; payable in New Zealand dollars before incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and New Zealand registered office service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent and company secretarial service provider in New Zealand
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a physical serviced office, statutory registers, and document acceptance; no statutory tariff applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, AML/CFT customer due diligence, and PEP/sanctions screening of all legal and natural persons
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand AML/CFT reportable entity or independent compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark based on identity verification, biometric checks, sanction database subscriptions, and enhanced due diligence reports; not a government fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Apostille or consular legalization bundle for five corporate instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand notary public, MFAT Authentication Unit, and destination state consular office where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: New Zealand notarial fee scale plus MFAT fixed fee per apostille/certificate and destination consulate fixed fee where consular legalization is required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal review of constitutional documents, registered office arrangements, and UBO disclosure under NZ trust and company law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly professional fee at prevailing New Zealand market rate for transactional corporate and AML compliance work; no statutory tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), in particular sections 13, 14, 15 and 20 (formation, incorporation, certificate of incorporation and company names), sections 42-48 (authority for issue of shares), section 128 (registered office), sections 149-156 (directors and consents), and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for the statutory secretarial and registered-agent licensing overlay
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online incorporation application) submitted through the New Zealand Companies Office e-incorporation portal, resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation of a company limited by shares
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company and no blocked escrow account rule. Shares may be allotted for any consideration or for no paid-up capital at formation, subject only to solvency and the constitution. If foreign ownership is involved, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening may apply only to specified land or sensitive assets, not to ordinary share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THIS FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION is made on [day] [month] [year] by and among the directors of [Company Name] (the Company), a company incorporated and registered under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand. The undersigned directors, constituting a quorum, unanimously resolve, certify and record as follows. 1. INCORPORATION AND CONSTITUTION. The board ratifies the incorporation of the Company, the grant of the Certificate of Incorporation by the Registrar of Companies, and the registration of the Company's constitution. The board confirms that the constitution filed in the incorporation application governs the internal affairs of the Company and that the Company is a company limited by shares. 2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The board accepts the subscription for the initial ordinary shares as recorded in the register of members and resolves that such shares be allotted, allotted as fully paid, or credited as fully paid in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution. The board confirms that the total issued capital is recorded in the directors' statement of solvency and that no minimum paid-up capital is required by law. 3. BANKING ARRANGEMENTS. The board designates [Authorised Bank and branch] in New Zealand as principal banker. The board authorizes the directors jointly and severally to open a corporate bank account, to execute account mandates, to negotiate credit facilities, to operate payment channels, and to sign all documents necessary for closure or transfer of accounts. All cheques, payment instructions and external financial obligations shall be signed by two authorized directors. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE. The board approves and adopts [physical address in New Zealand] as the Company's registered office and confirms that such office is open to the public during ordinary business hours on business days as required by the Companies Act 1993. The board directs the company secretary or compliance officer to file the registered office address, and any subsequent change of address, with the Registrar of Companies within ten working days. 5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints [Director A] as governing director and [Director B] as executive director. The board appoints [Name] as company secretary, regulatory filing agent and AML/CFT compliance officer for the Company's registered-agent and offshore secretarial services. The appointed officers are authorised to issue share certificates, maintain statutory registers, file all returns, register as a reporting entity where required, and manage client compliance files under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. 6. GENERAL PROVISIONS. This resolution is a permanent record of the board and may be certified and produced to banks, governmental authorities, auditors, counterparties and professional advisers. It takes effect immediately and remains in force until amended or revoked by a later board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Reservation and Preliminary Corporate Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office name reservation portal under the Registrar of Companies, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the New Zealand Companies Office name reservation portal and perform a two-part search of the Companies Register: first an exact-match search and then a confusingly similar or phonetic search. Submit the proposed company name and pay the applicable name reservation fee. If the name contains a restricted element such as trust, corporate, bank, or a personal surname, attach a signed consent letter from the relevant authority or person. Sign the name reservation application electronically using a RealMe login or, for manual lodgement, submit the prescribed notarised paper form. Use the approved name within the reservation period to avoid losing priority. The requested dossiers and the proposed constitution should be prepared before the reservation request is submitted.
required_dossiers: Completed company name reservation application
RealMe electronic signature or notarised paper form
Consent letters for restricted words if any
Certified copy of proposed directors identification
Proposed constitution draft
Statement of the principal business activity in ISIC code 8299
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office refuses or queries the name because it is offensive, unavailable, or confusingly similar, the applicant may select a new name or, within ten working days, file a request for reconsideration together with a written explanation or a consent letter from the holder of an existing identical or similar name. The reservation can then be reissued or modified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation Application and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office e-incorporation portal, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Office e-incorporation portal with the approved name reservation. Enter the full company name, registered office physical address, address for service, share structure and particulars of every director and shareholder. Attach the signed constitution and any consents to act as director. The portal verifies that at least one director is a natural person ordinarily resident in New Zealand or that an eligible Australian resident director arrangement is in place where applicable. Submit the application, pay the incorporation fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number automatically upon registration. Confirm the legal personality of the company and download the official certificate for subsequent bank, tax and licence applications.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation certificate or reference
Signed constitution
Consents to act as director from all proposed directors
Shareholder subscription and consent statements
Proof of physical registered office address such as lease or title record
Completed online incorporation application data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar issues a notice of defect or suspends the application, the applicant must respond in writing within the specified deadline with corrected data and supporting documents. If the application is rejected, incorporate a fresh application citing the same name if still valid or reserve an amended name. Judicial review under the High Court Rules is available as an ultimate remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, NZBN Activation and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand and the authorised New Zealand banking institution chosen by the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the New Zealand Business Number issued on the Certificate of Incorporation to register the company with Inland Revenue for an IRD number, PAYE, fringe benefit tax and GST if annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000. The board should then open a corporate bank account with an authorised New Zealand bank. Provide the certificate of incorporation, constitution, board resolution and certified identities of account signatories. Complete the bank's customer due diligence, including identifying beneficial owners and the source of funds. The board's two-director signing rule should be inserted into the bank mandate. Keep copies of the bank account opening forms in the company's statutory records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number confirmation
IRD number application form and GST registration forms if applicable
Board banking resolution
Certified copies of directors and beneficial owners identification
Registered office lease or proof of physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue does not issue a number within the expected service level, the applicant may contact the IRD Business Link service or write to its Client Contact Centre. If a bank declines the application, the board should remedy the due-diligence gaps and submit a revised application to the same bank or an alternative bank. A formal complaint to the New Zealand Banking Ombudsman is available where refusal is unexplained or discriminatory.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Programme Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs, AML/CFT Group of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the company under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, which captures persons providing registered office, formation agent or company secretarial services as a regular course of business. If so, register the business with the Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT Group. Appoint a senior manager or director as the AML/CFT compliance officer, conduct a business risk assessment covering money laundering and terrorism financing, develop the mandatory compliance programme and adopt customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting procedures. Submit the registration and supervisor notification and retain a copy of the risk assessment and compliance programme for audit.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT reporting entity registration form
Business risk assessment for money laundering and terrorism financing
AML/CFT compliance programme
Compliance officer appointment letter
Organisational chart and ownership details
Procedure manuals for registered-agent and offshore secretarial services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Internal Affairs asks questions or rejects the registration, remediate the compliance programme and resubmit within twenty working days. The supervisor may impose conditions; the company must remedy those conditions promptly, request an extension if necessary, and may seek an internal review or appeal to the enhanced regulatory action process where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Occupation, Statutory Registers and Annual Return Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies and the company's own corporate governance office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the registered office is a physical New Zealand street address, not a post office box, and that it is open for service of documents at the times required by the Companies Act. Populate the statutory registers, including the share register, director and shareholder interest registers, minute books and accounting records, and store them at the registered office or an approved place. Complete and stamp any share certificates and enter the issue of shares. Establish an annual return calendar so company returns are filed with the Companies Office before the balance date. For the ISIC 8299 business, implement client acceptance and record-retention procedures under the Privacy Act 2020.
required_dossiers: Leased or owned registered-office premises evidence
Notification of registered office address to Companies Office
Share certificates and register of members
Statutory register binders for directors and interests
Board minute book
Annual return calendar and compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office communicates a breach of the registered-office or annual-return obligation, remedy the non-compliance immediately by updating the registered address or filing a late return. Apply for late filing relief if available, and consider requesting a Registrar's correction if the address or return data was entered incorrectly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (Te Tari Taiwhenua), AML/CFT Group; for any physical premises, the territorial authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Reporting Entity Registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; no factory or industrial manufacturing permit applicable for ISIC 8299 registered-agent and offshore secretarial services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand (EPA) and the responsible regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / environmental registration only: no Schedule 1 or Schedule 2 prescribed industrial activity, no full Environmental Impact Assessment report and no resource consent required provided the activity is office-based and does not generate industrial discharges. If the operator later adds physical storage or light assembly, a separate resource consent and civil defence assessment may become necessary.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure office and consulting use; no wastewater, VOC or hazardous-waste discharge thresholds are triggered. If the company occupies a commercial office with an emergency generator, the generator exhaust must comply with the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) 2004 and PM10 concentrations must remain within the applicable regional plan limits. Any asbestos removal must follow the Health and Safety at Work (Asbestos) Regulations 2016.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Building Warrant of Fitness and Fire Safety Certificate for the occupied premises under the Building Act 2004; annual fire evacuation procedures and safety checks as required by Fire and Emergency New Zealand; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 worker engagement, first aid, welfare and hazards register; and Civil Defence Emergency Management Act 2002 business continuity measures applicable to registered-agent and secretarial office operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD) of New Zealand; online portal: myIR at ird.govt.nz. Entity formation also requires registration with the New Zealand Companies Office and allocation of a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the NZ_LTD company: (1) incorporate through the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993, obtaining a company number and NZBN; (2) apply to Inland Revenue via myIR for an IRD number, providing the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director and shareholder particulars, consent-to-act forms for non-resident officers, and bank account information for refunds; (3) apply for GST registration through the same myIR channel or separately where only GST obligations apply. For a foreign non-resident entity not incorporated in New Zealand but making supplies subject to NZ GST, the non-resident registers for an IRD number and GST using non-resident registration procedures in myIR, submitting equivalent foreign entity identification and proof of nexus. There is no minimum capital requirement and non-resident ownership is permitted for NZ limited companies, but a New Zealand registered office and a resident agent or director must be maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a New Zealand limited company is a separate corporate tax payer assessed on worldwide income; there is no default pass-through classification and no export free-zone standalone tax classification).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to a US check-the-box regime. New Zealand law provides a consolidated group election for wholly-owned company groups under the Income Tax Act 2007 and a GST grouping election under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid mismatch rules apply as mandatory statute, not as elective classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period for compulsory registration; voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand resident consumers are required to register and account for GST once their taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, no government API pre-approval, and no anti-fraud digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary in New Zealand, with the Peppol infrastructure used when taxpayers opt in. Tax invoices must contain the content required by the GST Act 1985, and GST returns and payments are submitted electronically to Inland Revenue through myIR.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, goods physically exported from New Zealand are eligible for the 0% GST rate when the supplier or a person on the supplier's behalf exports the goods and proper evidence of export is retained. Supplies of services to non-residents may be zero-rated under the offshore services rules if the services are performed and consumed outside New Zealand and are not caught by the New Zealand land/property or goods exceptions. For an ISIC 8299 registered-agent and offshore secretarial business, corporate secretarial, compliance and administrative services supplied to an overseas client for use wholly outside New Zealand are treated as exported services eligible for zero-rating when the non-resident status of the recipient and the offshore consumption are documented. Remote/digital services to non-resident consumers likewise follow the destination principle; in all cases, the taxpayer must retain the statutory evidence before claiming 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service electronic Export Entry lodged through the Trade Single Window clearly linking the exporter, consignee, goods value and export movement
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from New Zealand customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported goods and the sales contract

Bank payment or remittance records, settlement advice or foreign currency conversion statement showing the foreign buyer's actual payment (New Zealand does not issue a statutory FIRC; equivalent bank FX records are retained as the forex repatriation evidence)
Carrier statement, container tracking record or port/airport release documentation corroborating the outbound movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue matches GST returns, NZCS export entries, carrier records and banking data to verify exports. If a 0% GST export claim is unsupported, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 15% GST and the unpaid tax is clawed back. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position and 150% for evasion; use-of-money interest runs from the original GST due date, and criminal prosecution may follow for fraudulent or knowingly false export zero-rating documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully convertible currency regime. The New Zealand Dollar is free-floating and traded actively in global offshore markets. There are no exchange control laws requiring central bank approval for current account or capital account transactions. Residents and non-residents may freely transfer funds in and out of the country subject only to general anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism verification requirements. The Reserve Bank, while supervising licensed banks, does not ration currency or impose surrender obligations. Dividends, management fees, and loan repayments can be remitted abroad without a foreign exchange license, provided underlying transactions are commercially genuine and comply with tax disclosure and New Zealand Inland Revenue obligations. For inbound direct investment, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 may require consent for certain sensitive land and significant business assets, but this is a foreign investment screening regime, not a currency control. Capital account transactions are equally open, with no central bank filing or pre-approval requirement beyond AML/CFT-induced documentation and financial institution risk tolerance. Therefore, liquidity planning focuses on banking counterparty access, SWIFT rails, tax withholding costs, and documentary integrity rather than currency convertibility constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand does not impose any statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings indefinitely, hold them in foreign currency accounts, or convert them to New Zealand Dollars at commercial market rates. There is no prescribed timeline for conversion and no Reserve Bank of New Zealand reporting obligation unless the transaction is subject to separate AML/CFT threshold reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD) with global multicurrency facilities
Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD) plus USD/EUR settlement sub-accounts
Capital Escrow Account for inbound equity injections and operational account
Capital Escrow Account and trade finance clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs are not legally barred from serving New Zealand entities, but their practical viability is low-to-medium for this corporate secretarial structure. EMIs must register on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register but do not hold a banking licence, cannot accept NZD deposits, and lack direct access to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand settlement system or domestic sort-code clearing. They can provide convenient multi-currency IBANs, virtual accounts, and payment cards for secondary disbursements, but they are not suitable as the primary treasury rail for a medium-risk enhanced company secretarial entity. A licensed domestic Tier-1 bank is mandatory for capital escrow, genuine trade settlement, and FX hedging due to credit and regulatory certainty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks generally require physical or supervised identity verification for directors and beneficial owners. A statutory director may appear in-branch, or identity can be verified by a New Zealand registered lawyer, accountant, or notary public using certified copies and live video confirmation. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted on a discretionary basis, but registered agent and offshore secretarial entities will be escalated to enhanced due diligence with a mandatory video interview, certified trust deed evidence, and original apostilled corporate documents before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office overlap and mass appointment of secretarial companies used to obscure multiple corporate clients from the same physical address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide tax residency certificates, board meeting minutes, business risk assessment of the client base, segregation of duties policy, lease agreement for the New Zealand registered office, staff employment records, and sample engagement contracts showing genuine commercial purpose for each underlying client entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain exceeding two tiers through a New Zealand nominee secretary and an offshore trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a full beneficial ownership register under the Companies Act 1993, supply the original trust deed and statement of purpose, letter of authorization from the settlor, independent source-of-wealth declaration, certified extract of the trust register, and a legal attestation from the New Zealand law firm that conducted the company secretarial formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and prohibited business exposure from payables and receivables routing through or from high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver adverse media and sanctions screening reports from a reputable data vendor such as Dow Jones or Refinitiv covering all counterparties and sub-accounts, transaction route ledgers matching the ISIC 8299 registered agent business model, bank referral letters for low-AML-rating jurisdictions, and the statutory business license for registered company secretarial operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large unexplained intercompany fund flows inconsistent with expected registered agent fee income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements, management accounts, transfer pricing documentation, payroll records showing actual staff in New Zealand, Inland Revenue GST returns, cash flow narrative with balance sheet reconciliation, and detailed invoices matching directory and secretarial fees for each client entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital' or 'Equity Injection'. Instruct the receiving New Zealand Tier-1 bank to book the inflow as share subscription proceeds in a capital escrow account. No New Zealand exchange control approval is required. The company must issue a board resolution for the share allotment under the Companies Act 1993 and provide a capital verification certificate from a New Zealand chartered accountant within 10 business days. The beneficial owner must submit a source-of-funds letter and bank statement showing traced wealth origin.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements will use SWIFT MT103 for cleared funds, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 for high-value import or export contracts, and Documentary Collections for lower-risk trade shipments. No foreign exchange license is needed. Banks will verify invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations to maintain the AML/CFT audit trail. The clearing rail should be selected based on transaction size, counterparty credit quality, and documentary complexity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD and NZD/EUR forward contracts with licensed domestic Tier-1 banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when the underlying settlement currency is non-convertible outside New Zealand and no onshore deliverable market is available
Cross-currency swaps between NZD and USD/EUR for maturities up to five years, subject to bank credit approval and the existence of a real economic exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company and annual confirmation of directors, shareholders, registered office, and address-for-service particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of the date of incorporation, unless the Registrar prescribes a different filing date; reminder notices are sent to the registered office before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable to fines of up to NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,200); continued default for six months or more permits the Registrar to issue notice under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993 and to strike the company off the register after 20 working days unless an objection is upheld.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and, where non-exempt, the independent auditor's report filed with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (only for companies that are not exempt from public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance date for FMC reporting entities, large companies, and other companies required to publicly file; exempt private companies are generally not required to file financial statements with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply may result in infringement notices, court-imposed monetary penalties against the company and directors, and remedial enforcement action by the Registrar; persistent non-compliance may expose the company to removal from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all FMC reporting entities, licensed insurers, registered banks, and companies classified as large under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, generally where group total assets exceed NZD 60 million or group total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million; small private companies may also be required to obtain an audit by shareholder direction or board resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), comprising full NZ IFRS for Tier 1, NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2, and simplified Tier 3 standards for small entities, as issued by the External Reporting Board

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual ultimate beneficial ownership return for a private limited company; the Annual Return confirms all shareholders of record, directors, and any shareholding changes. A transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next Annual Return. As a licensed registered agent and AML/CFT reporting entity, beneficial owners must be identified and verified at engagement and re-confirmed upon any material change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not operate a statutory tax holiday regime. The headline 28% company rate is mitigated through the imputation credit regime, a 15% R&D tax incentive credit, certain inter-corporate dividend exemptions, and a perpetual tax-loss carry-forward framework that is subject to shareholder continuity and business continuity requirements. No zero-rate concession applies to the ISIC 8299_01 registered-agent and offshore secretarial business segment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR Secure Online Services or through a commercial tax intermediary approved by Inland Revenue.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July of the same calendar year. Tax agents operating under an extension arrangement may defer the filing due date, typically to 31 March of the following year; provisional tax instalment obligations remain payable on their statutory due dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRD number, legal name, registered office, postal address, and accounting balance date of the NZ limited company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned NZ Ltd is still a New Zealand resident company for tax purposes and must file using its NZ IRD number. Non-resident ultimate shareholders are not separately registered unless the NZ Ltd is acting as a non-resident company's branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived from the registered-agent, company-secretarial, and administrative-service business, including fees, commissions, and other gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ-resident company must declare its worldwide income unless a foreign income exemption or CFC rule applies. A non-resident company carrying on a business through a NZ branch would include only New Zealand-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All permissible deductions, including operating expenses, office costs, professional fees, salaries, depreciation, interest, and AML/CFT compliance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred in deriving assessable income and must satisfy the general permission and apportionment rules. Payments to overseas affiliates must be arm's-length and disclosed to Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or net loss computed as gross income less deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the NZ Ltd operates purely as a pass-through secretarial shell, Inland Revenue will examine whether the losses are being used to shelter foreign revenue; the company must support all allocations with documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses applied against current-year net income, subject to continuity of ownership and business continuity tests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign parents, shareholder continuity of at least 49% must be maintained through the period; a breakdown in continuity extinguishes loss carry-forward rights and must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 – Box 6 (Taxable income after loss offset)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual taxable income after applying available loss carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ-resident company must reconcile this amount with its statutory financial statements and IR10 financial summary to avoid discrepancies flagged by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base corporate income tax calculated by applying 28% to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch of a foreign company is taxed at the same 28% rate on New Zealand-sourced income, while a non-resident shareholder is not subject to company tax on the NZ Ltd's retained earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 – Box 8 (Credits: RWT, provisional tax, foreign tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax credits, provisional tax payments, imputation credits, and foreign tax credits used to settle the income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders should attach a tax residence certificate to support any treaty credit claim. The NZ company must not claim credits for tax withheld on distributions to non-residents because NRWT operates separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net income tax payable to Inland Revenue or refundable excess credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before approval, shareholders must confirm that any dividend distribution to non-residents has triggered non-resident withholding tax at the applicable statutory or treaty-reduced rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an IR4 return attracts a late filing penalty of NZD 50. Unpaid tax accrues a late payment penalty of 1% immediately, followed by 1.5% per month during continued default, plus use-of-money interest at the quarterly statutory rate applied daily to the unpaid balance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (non-resident withholding tax on gross dividends paid by a NZ-resident company to a non-resident shareholder; reduced treaty rates often apply, commonly to 15% under New Zealand's double tax agreements)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit a valid tax residence certificate from its home-country competent authority to the NZ payer before the dividend payment. The NZ payer retains that certificate, confirms beneficial ownership, applies the reduced treaty withholding rate, and discloses the payment on the IR37A NRWT return. Where the DTA includes a Principal Purpose Test or Limitation on Benefits clause, additional substance evidence must be held. A New Zealand company requesting a certificate of residence for overseas treaty claims uses Inland Revenue form IR290.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT rates are 15% for royalties and 15% for interest. Comprehensive DTAs typically reduce interest and royalty withholding to 10%, with certain treaties at 5% or lower. Qualifying interest on listed approved debt securities may instead be subject to the 2% Approved Issuer Levy where the lender is not associated and the approved issuer conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions (this threshold is the Inland Revenue risk-based expectation for contemporaneous documentation; no explicit general statutory minimum exists, but documentation is essential for shortfall penalty relief under the Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the Tax Administration Act 1994).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, the Companies Act 1993 requires a registered office, a director, and proper accounting records in New Zealand. For tax purposes, the general anti-avoidance rule in Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1, controlled foreign company rules, and transfer pricing rules operate to recharacterise artificial arrangements lacking real commercial substance. An entity in the ISIC 8299_01 registered-agent and offshore secretarial sector must additionally satisfy AML/CFT reporting-entity obligations and demonstrate genuine client-administration functions to avoid being treated as a shell or conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false IR4 return, understating gross income, overstating deductible expenses, omitting offshore bank accounts, destroying accounting records, or creating sham invoices for company-secretarial and registered-agent services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall under Tax Administration Act 1994; criminal prosecution under section 143B exposes individuals to imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to NZD 50,000, while a body corporate may be fined up to NZD 200,000 for each offence; use-of-money interest and late payment penalties also accrue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate or knowingly assist in the filing of false returns are personally exposed to criminal prosecution and may be disqualified from managing companies under Companies Act 1993. Inland Revenue may obtain a departure prohibition order preventing a director from leaving New Zealand while significant unpaid tax liabilities remain.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand limited company as a mailbox entity with no real office, employees, business records, or substantive decision-making, while using the company to access New Zealand's tax treaty network, imputation credits, or domestic withholding tax exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may apply the general anti-avoidance rule, disregard the corporate structure, recharacterise income, and deny treaty benefits under the Multinational Instrument Principal Purpose Test. Shortfall penalties of up to 50% apply for an abusive tax position, increasing to 150% for evasion. Repeated failure to maintain a genuinely operative registered office can lead to company deregistration under the Companies Act 1993.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who use a shell company as a facade may be jointly and severally assessed on the adjusted taxable income. Inland Revenue may pursue civil recovery against directors personally, impose management bans, and use asset-restraint or departure-prohibition measures where tax debts are being stripped through dividend distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, royalties, or interest between the NZ Ltd and its overseas parent or affiliates without preparing contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, benchmarking, or functional and risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will recompute taxable income under the arm's-length principle. Penalties range from 20% of the tax shortfall for failure to take reasonable care or adopting an unacceptable tax position, 50% for an abusive tax avoidance position, and 150% for evasion. The disallowed payments may be recharacterised as non-deductible distributions or dividends subject to NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve transfer pricing declarations without reasonable care can be subject to shortfall penalties in their capacity as tax filers. In fraud cases, veil-piercing may occur, making directors personally liable for the tax shortfall and applicable penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder or lender without deducting non-resident withholding tax, mislabelling distributions as inter-company management fees, or stripping profits through excessive interest without satisfying thin-capitalisation rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unremitted NRWT becomes a debt due to the Crown; the payer is subject to shortfall penalties, late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest. For deliberate evasion, criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 applies. The statutory rates are 30% for dividends and 15% for interest and royalties, unless a reduced treaty rate or Approved Issuer Levy applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for withheld or deductible tax that the company fails to remit, especially where the company is liquidated and the Crown is an unsecured creditor. If a director knowingly participates in a scheme to strip assets and avoid NRWT, the corporate veil may be pierced and travel bans or imprisonment imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing registered-agent, company-secretarial, or nominee-director services without maintaining an AML/CFT compliance programme, failing to conduct customer due diligence and identify beneficial owners, or failing to report suspicious transactions in respect of offshore nominee structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a body corporate can face civil penalties of up to NZD 2 million for a significant contravention, and individuals can face criminal penalties including imprisonment for up to 7 years for money laundering offences. The statutory supervisor may suspend or cancel the reporting entity's registration and issue enforceable remediation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and senior managers who knowingly participate in laundering proceeds of crime are exposed to personal criminal liability and imprisonment. They may also be disqualified as officers of reporting entities, banned from managing companies, and subjected to civil asset-recovery proceedings and travel restrictions.
